(Disclosure up front: I did not finish this turd. I gave up around page 100. If someone wants to provide an example of how things suddenly became awesome, I mean Kung Fu Panda awesome, around page 101, please let me know.)

There are first published novels, and there are first published novels. In the former category are Dan Simmons' Song of Kali, Stephen King's Carrie, Richard Adams' Watership Down, Umberto Eco's The Name of the Rose.

This one is in the latter category.

And it's so bloody frustrating to say that, because the subject matter you wish somebody would write about competently. It's a story about gods living in downtown Hong Kong, in particular, the god who invented martial arts, and their battles against (what else?) Eastern demons. The mythology (if not cosmology) you get in the book is fascinating, and Chan tries pretty hard -- as a former resident of Hong Kong -- to inject local nuance, colour, culture, etc, into the book.

But oh my Jesus it's written like a teenager's fucking fan fiction. The protagonist (100 pages in) is bland as only authors inserting themselves into their stories can be. Bella Swan in Twilight was Hamlet-level complex next to this one. Naturally the god (who has flowing black hair and dresses up in old-fashioned Chinese clothes, of course) starts to fall in love with her. And there's a token black dude in the story (and for extra points, he's explicitly gay for no apparent reason connected with the story). They withhold the big reveal of what the god is well past the point of competent storytelling. Seriously, there are so many "I'll tell you laters" here you'd think they were telling the old joke "How do you keep an idiot in suspense". Small child is introduced into the story as blatant Macguffin. Fight scenes are not gripping and written about as convincingly as a man writing the blow-by-blows of childbirth from a woman's perspective. At least I got out before any sex scenes started happening.

So. Bloody. Frustrating. Such a missed opportunity. You have no soul if you didn't like Big Trouble In Little China, and this could have been an awesome ride, but, avoid it.
